findings.title: SQL Error Disclosure via client_id Parameter in OAuth Token Endpoint
findings.description: The /oauth/token endpoint leaks Hibernate SQLGrammarException errors when an invalid client_id is provided. The client_id parameter is injected directly into a database query. All 5 tested invalid client_id values trigger SQL exceptions, confirming the parameter reaches the database unsanitized. This was reproduced from a completely unauthenticated, cookie-free session.

poc_steps.request:
POST /oauth/token HTTP/1.1
Host: op-api-uat-ap1.shijicloud.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=test&client_id=shijimini&client_secret=123456
poc_steps.response:
HTTP/1.1 401
SQLGrammarException: could not extract ResultSet — Hibernate SQL error leaked in response body

HTTP/1.1 401
SQLGrammarException confirmed for ALL non-existent client_id values

HTTP/1.1 401
Same SQL error — parameter directly injected into database query

impacts: Database query structure exposed via Hibernate exception messages
Client-side parameter injected into backend SQL without sanitization
Reproducible from unauthenticated, zero-cookie session
Enables SQL injection exploitation if WAF bypass payloads succeed
findings.remediation: Validate client_id against a whitelist before database lookup. Use parameterized queries instead of string concatenation. Return generic 401 without exposing internal exception details.

findings.title: Swagger UI + Swagger Resources Publicly Accessible Without Authentication
findings.description: The full Swagger UI interface and /swagger-resources endpoint are publicly accessible without any authentication. The resources endpoint exposes 3 API groups (ac, system, minipos) with their v2/api-docs paths, providing a complete API attack surface map to unauthenticated users.

poc_steps.response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Full Swagger UI rendered — Springfox v2.10.0

impacts: Complete API inventory exposed to unauthenticated attackers
3 microservice groups enumerated
Combined with JS source analysis reveals 32+ API endpoints
findings.remediation: Restrict /swagger-ui.html and /swagger-resources to authenticated sessions only. Disable Swagger entirely in production environments.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoint
findings.description: The /oauth/login endpoint accepts unlimited consecutive failed authentication attempts without rate limiting, 429 responses, or account lockout. Tested with 10 rapid failed attempts — all accepted within seconds.

poc_steps.request:
POST /oauth/login (10 times rapidly)
wrong_password each time
poc_steps.response: All 10 attempts return HTTP 500 (not 429). No rate limiting headers present.

impacts: Enables credential brute-force attacks
No account lockout after repeated failures
Common bug bounty finding — validated per program requirements
findings.remediation: Implement rate limiting: 5 failures per IP/minute, account lockout after 10 failures, CAPTCHA after 3 failures.

findings.title: Token Not Invalidated After Logout, No Concurrent Session Limit
findings.description: After calling GET /system/logout which returns HTTP 302, the access token remains fully valid. Additionally, generating 3 concurrent login sessions produces 3 independently valid tokens that can be used simultaneously without any session limit enforcement.

poc_steps.response: HTTP 200 — token still valid after logout!

poc_steps.request: 3 concurrent login calls → 3 tokens generated → all 3 valid simultaneously
poc_steps.response: All 3 tokens return HTTP 200 on protected endpoints

impacts: Stolen tokens persist after user logout
Multiple concurrent sessions bypass session management
Token expires_in: 12 hours — long window for abuse
findings.remediation: Implement server-side token revocation on logout. Limit concurrent sessions per user. Reduce token expiry time to 1 hour with refresh rotation.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers Across All 3 In-Scope Targets
findings.description: All three in-scope targets are missing critical security headers. Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy are absent on all targets. The API gateway also lacks Content-Security-Policy.

poc_steps.response: Missing: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy across all 3. API also missing CSP.

impacts: MITM downgrade possible (no HSTS)
MIME sniffing attacks possible (no X-Content-Type-Options)
Referrer leakage to third parties (no Referrer-Policy)
findings.remediation: Add HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin on all targets.

findings.title: Nginx Server Version Disclosure
findings.description: The Web and Identity servers expose nginx/1.25.3 in the Server response header, enabling attackers to check for version-specific CVEs and vulnerabilities.

poc_steps.request: HEAD / HTTP/1.1 on web and identity servers

impacts: Enables targeted attacks using known nginx 1.25.3 vulnerabilities
findings.remediation: Set server_tokens off; in nginx configuration.

findings.title: Opaque 500 Errors on Invalid Authentication (Information Disclosure)
findings.description: All failed login attempts return HTTP 500 with {"code":"500","msg":"System Error","traceId":"..."} instead of a proper HTTP 401 with clean error messaging. The traceId leaks internal request tracking identifiers.
impacts: Internal traceId values leaked to unauthenticated users
Cannot differentiate between 'system down' and 'wrong password' for incident response
Non-standard error handling exposes internal implementation details
findings.remediation: Return HTTP 401 with {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Invalid credentials"} for authentication failures.

findings.title: JSESSIONID Cookie Missing Secure and HttpOnly Flags
findings.description: The API gateway sets JSESSIONID cookie without Secure or HttpOnly flags.
impacts: Cookie vulnerable to MITM interception (no Secure flag)
Cookie accessible via XSS (no HttpOnly flag)
findings.remediation: Set Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict on all session cookies.

findings.title: Hardcoded OAuth Client Secret in JavaScript Bundle
findings.description: The web application JavaScript contains client_secret=123456 for the OAuth refresh token flow: grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=X&client_id=client&client_secret=123456.
impacts: If refresh token endpoint does not validate client_secret, enables session hijacking
findings.remediation: Never store secrets in client-side JavaScript. Use backend-to-backend communication for OAuth token exchange.

verified_not_vulnerable: Actuator detail endpoints (/env, /mappings, /heapdump) — properly auth-gated (401 on clean session)
CORS configuration — no arbitrary origin reflection with credentials
User enumeration timing — not statistically significant (0.2σ)
Scope escalation — token scope fixed to 'app'
Password policy — weak passwords properly rejected
